name: Plan 9 from Outer Space

rappel_detail.notes: First rappel from the Blob's summit ridge over a steep step at the edge of the Blob/Terror col.
Second rappel continuing down into the notch below; from the notch an easy scramble down the col returns climbers to the bench.

rappels: 2 rappels from the summit ridge into the Blob–Terror col notch, then downclimb/scramble back to camp
descent_text: From the top, traverse the summit ridge of the Blob northward toward the Blob/Terror col — an adventure in its own right, with short simul-climbing recommended over the exposed crest. At the col edge, locate webbing rappel anchors over a steep step and make two rappels down into the notch. From the notch, an easy scramble down the col returns climbers to the bench below.
approach: From the Goodell Creek group-camp trailhead near Newhalem, walk the overgrown Goodell Creek roadbed for about 4 miles to the cairn near the Terror Creek crossing, then climb the Terror Creek climbers' path. The Blob stands above Crescent Creek Basin, so from the Terror Creek side you must cross the Barrier, the loose, brushy ridge dividing the Terror Creek drainage from Crescent Creek; it can be crossed low or high from Terror Basin. Descend into Crescent Creek Basin and camp within reach of the Himmelhorn and the Blob, then scramble to the base of the south buttress. This is a serious multi-day expedition approach requiring a North Cascades National Park backcountry permit, off-trail routefinding through brush and talus, and glacier/snow travel gear.
overview: A long, moderate alpine rock line up the right-edge buttress of "The Blob," the rock formation just north of the Himmelhorn in the Southern Pickets, finishing across the exposed "Bela Lugosi Traverse" and up a summit dihedral.
beta: Plan 9 from Outer Space climbs roughly 16 pitches (~1,400 ft) of varied, mostly moderate rock up the right edge of a prominent buttress on "The Blob." The route crosses the exposed-but-moderate "Bela Lugosi Traverse" below a large ledge, then finishes up a steep dihedral of good rock to the summit. The first-ascent party rated the crux 5.10c; a repeat ascent found an easier line and down-rated it to 5.9, and the route is now given a compromise grade of 5.9+ — as with many alpine routes of this style, the felt difficulty depends heavily on which exact line you choose.
gear: cams to 3 inch (doubles in common sizes)
face: South Buttress of The Blob (aka The Rake)
